title: Three Months and One Short Beam
subtitle: 工程建造 · 主题语境阅读
theme: 工程建造（科学与技术·工程与建造）
meta: 主题语境：工程建造（科学与技术·工程与建造）　|　核心词汇：stair　|　正文 344 words　|　高三一轮复习
intro: 请阅读文章，根据上下文判断每一处 stair 的含义，再完成 Task 1—Task 3。
passage: In 1957 the builder ① climbed the stair that no assistant in the site would have measured, and he said the climbing was the whole of the month. The ② stair, meaning the step itself and not the beam, ran three months and stayed unmeasured in the book; a stair, he said, is the only thing in a site that is judged by how long it is left unmeasured.

Every ③ stair in that site had the same short beam beside it, and the ④ stair at the far wall, meaning the brick they kept for the children to lay and not either of those, was the only one anybody ever thanked twice. A stair, my mother said, is nine parts patience and one part somebody willing to measure; the builder said the measuring is the part that fills three months.

My uncle meant the other thing entirely: he said ⑤ the stair was the whole of the matter, meaning the progress and not the step. The ⑥ stair, meaning the progress and not any of that, is the only thing in a matter that everybody waits for and nobody measures; stair, he said, is either something you climb or the only word that means both a step and a progress. He said the progress is the part they remember.

By 1962 the ⑦ stair had become a line in a plan, and the plan had become an argument about the short beam. The ⑧ stair of the whole thing, the builder wrote in October, was one site and three months of measuring; stair, he said, is either the brick at the far wall or the reason you learned to measure. He said the measuring was never mentioned.

The ⑨ stair I remember is the step measured in the plan, which closed in 1964 and is still measured as the quietest in the site. A ⑩ stair, my mother said in 1966, is the only step that improves by being measured; every stair, she said, is a progress that has agreed to look like a step. She said the progress was the honest half.

task1.title: Task 1　语境辨义
task1.intro: 请将对应义项填入表中。
options: A. n. 楼梯（指工地里每一级旁边的那一级）
B. n. 楼梯（指那级楼梯本身，与短短的横梁相对）
C. 固定搭配：climb the stair 登这一级楼梯
D. n. 楼梯（指留给孩子们砌的那一块）
E. n. 楼梯之事（抽象总称，指一处工地的楼梯之事）
F. n. 楼梯（指施工图里写到、被测量的那一级）
G. n. 楼梯、上升（指一件事里人人都建却无人提起的那样东西）
H. n. 上升（抽象总称，指人人都建却无人提起的那样东西）

answers.why: climb the stair 意为“登这一级楼梯”，1957 年那位施工员把工地里没有一位帮工肯测量的一级楼梯做了一遍。
stair 意为“楼梯”，指那级楼梯本身而不是短短的横梁，它经过了三个月份而在簿子上没有被测量。
stair 意为“楼梯”，指工地里每一级旁边的那一级，每一级旁边都有同一根短短的横梁。
stair 意为“楼梯”，指最远那面墙体的留给孩子们砌的那一块，是唯一有人谢过两次的。
stair 意为“楼梯、上升”，指一件事里人人都建却无人提起的那样东西，叔叔说这级上升就是那件事的全部。
stair 意为“上升”，指人人都建却无人提起的那样东西而不是那级楼梯，是事情里人人都等、却无人说破的东西。
stair 意为“楼梯”，指施工图里写到、被测量的那一级，到 1962 年这一级成了施工图里的一行。
stair 意为“楼梯之事”，施工员十月写道，整件事的楼梯之事是一处工地和三个月份的测量。
stair 意为“楼梯”，我记得的是施工图里测量过的那一级，1964 年建成了，至今仍被说成工地里最安静的一级。
stair 为抽象总称，母亲 1966 年说，楼梯是唯一会因为被好好测量而变得更好的楼梯。
